entries.old: Render a desktop newsroom SVG only after deterministic lint passes. The phone-facing mobile page is off by default; set NEWSROOM_MOBILE_PAGES=1 to render the mobile variant too. The SQL is rerun and its canonical row hash must match the linted data snapshot before publication artifacts are written.
entries.new: Render a desktop newsroom SVG only after deterministic lint passes. The phone-facing mobile page is not produced. The SQL is rerun and its canonical row hash must match the linted data snapshot before publication artifacts are written.

entries.old: Review the rendered desktop newsroom viewport after deterministic lint (the phone-facing mobile page is off by default; set NEWSROOM_MOBILE_PAGES=1 to also render and critique mobile). The critic scores editorial hierarchy, density, highlighting, annotations, direct labeling, accessibility, and source visibility, then persists repair suggestions for another agent revision when needed.

entries.old: Render a desktop semantic explanatory SVG after lint passes. The phone-facing mobile page is off by default; set NEWSROOM_MOBILE_PAGES=1 to render the mobile variant too.
entries.new: Render a desktop semantic explanatory SVG after lint passes. The phone-facing mobile page is not produced.

entries.old: Invoke a configured shell-free illustration adapter using a stdin JSON to stdout JSON contract. The adapter must return a desktop SVG variant plus origin metadata; the newsroom sanitizes active SVG content, enforces origin policy, hashes the bytes and persists disclosure metadata. The phone-facing mobile page is off by default, so any mobile variant the adapter returns is discarded; set NEWSROOM_MOBILE_PAGES=1 to keep it.

entries.old: Rasterize the exact content-addressed desktop page SVG and return it as an image tool result so the active multimodal provider can inspect the composed page. The phone-facing mobile page is off by default, so only the desktop image is returned; set NEWSROOM_MOBILE_PAGES=1 to also observe mobile. A passing deterministic infographic critic is required first.

The phone-facing mobile page is not produced, so only the desktop image is returned. A passing deterministic infographic critic is required first.
Score and every rubric item are on a 0-100 scale. The page passes only when score is at least 80, every rubric item is at least 60 and no issue is a blocker; set passed=false if any of these fails.

entries.old: The phone-facing mobile page is off by default. Omit breakpoints for the desktop-only default, or pass exactly [1440]; any other width set is rejected.

entries.new: The program sets the browser-check width (1440), the page-size limit and the ready-time limit. Do not pass breakpoints, max_initial_bytes or max_ready_ms: a call that does is refused.
If the user asks for one chart, pair it with one explanatory module (illustration, map or cutaway), not a second chart of the same kind.
Modules of type d3 cannot draw in this build because no D3 runtime ships; use type plotly instead (sankey is available as plotly).

Chart kind of the module. Modules of type d3 cannot draw in this build because no D3 runtime ships; use type plotly instead (sankey is available as plotly). A d3 module needs one of: radial_network, radial_hierarchy, circle_packing, sankey, chord, edge_bundle, beeswarm, parallel_coordinates. A plotly module takes one of: statistical, sankey, scattergl, parallel_coordinates, sunburst, treemap, icicle, surface3d, network, scientific_map, geo_linked (statistical when omitted); when it is bound by computation_ref only statistical, sankey, treemap, sunburst, icicle, parallel_coordinates, geo_linked are built. geo_linked is the point map (lon/lat or ISO-3 location fields). Any other value on a d3 or plotly module is refused when the page is rendered.

Width on the page's 12-column grid: full = 12 of 12 columns, wide = 8 of 12 columns, half = 6 of 12 columns, third = 4 of 12 columns. When omitted the module is third (4 of 12 columns, one third of the width); pass full for a chart that needs the room.

entries.old: Resolve immutable publication bindings, reverify row hashes and sanitized assets, then render the PublicationSpec. The renderer never accepts fresh inline data.
entries.new: Resolve immutable publication bindings, reverify row hashes and sanitized assets, then render the PublicationSpec. The renderer never accepts fresh inline data. The page style is resolved here from the modules' explanatory_dimension (spatial -> geography; mechanism/model -> process_graph; flow -> flow_edges; network/relationship -> graph_edges; hierarchy -> hierarchy; every other dimension -> tabular; stat and text modules are skipped). The render is refused with "Style mapping blocked" when the style profile (the style_profile given to newsroom_publication_plan, or the automatic choice) does not list every dimension and topology on the page. newsroom_style_map checks the same rule; it is not a required step, but call it before the plan when the page mixes several of these dimensions. When omitted: standalone_visual.

Category or series values drawn in the one accent colour, for the chart types that paint it. When omitted nothing is highlighted. On a world-map choropleth they instead choose extra labelled countries.

Style profile; when omitted the program picks it from the modules' explanatory_dimension values, first match wins: uncertainty -> uncertainty_forecast; network -> investigative_network; spatial -> spatial_monitor; flow/mechanism/model -> systems_explainer; none of these -> analytical_precision.
Delivery mode (html, scrollytelling, hybrid); when omitted: html.
Page language; when omitted the page is en: lang and the renderer's own labels follow it.

Quality bar (publishable: critic score at least 88 and every rubric dimension at least 72; award: critic score at least 92 and every rubric dimension at least 78; award also adds further checks); when omitted: publishable.
Layout and checks look only at whether the value is hero. When omitted, the step that fills hero stats treats the module as secondary; elsewhere an omitted value just means not hero.

Used only when the lean gate is on (NEWSROOM_LEAN_GATES=1) and schema_version is 1.4.0 or 1.5.0: a module without reader_question_id, claim set, new_information, explanatory_dimension is left out of the semantic-novelty comparison and counted in a note.
